## Choose the smallest environment

| Work | Needed locally | External boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Docs, navigation, inventory | Node/Bun, repository files | Network only for first pinned Mintlify download |
| Utility, route-policy, and mocked service tests | Bun and installed dependencies | Fixtures replace the documented boundaries |
| Next.js app/UI development | Bun, the owning Next app, required app env | Approved hosted dev/staging services when needed |
| Database integration or migration application | Isolated Supabase/Postgres fixture | Approved remote devbox or a disposable test database |
| Hosted cron diagnosis | Read access to owning workflow/provider telemetry | Vercel/Cloudflare and the deployed processor |
| Native mobile work | Flutter/platform tooling | Product providers and approved test services |

Docker setup, the Docker cron runner, Rust, and TanStack Start are not required
for the active path. A particular database/container integration test may still
need an isolated container runtime; offload that test rather than treating it as
a requirement for every task. Fixtures do not prove a real database migration or
hosted media network works.

## Install and run an active app

Use the repository's pinned Bun and Node requirements from the
[version reference](/reference/repository/versions):

```bash
bun install --frozen-lockfile
```

Use the owning app's documented environment variables and an approved dev/staging
service configuration. Keep values in ignored local env files. A remote database
URL is not permission to change production data. Do not require `bun setup` for
minimal onboarding: it can build packages and probe Docker/local services.

When runtime development is needed, start only the selected Next app, for example
`bun dev:web` or `bun dev:calendar`. Portless provides the established app host
and central-login boundary. The package's `dev:app` is available for direct-port
work, but cross-app auth still needs valid local origins and coordinated URLs.
Do not start Rust or TanStack Start merely to satisfy an old setup paragraph.

## Preview documentation locally

```bash
bun dev:docs
```

This runs `scripts/local-docs.js` from the repository root. It executes the
pinned Mintlify CLI through `npx` in `apps/docs` and needs no Docker daemon,
Compose stack, database, Rust, or TanStack Start. The CLI pin is read from `apps/docs/mintlify-version.json`, independently of
retained Docker configuration.
The first run downloads that version; later runs can reuse the npm cache.
Stop the foreground preview with Ctrl+C.

For another port or a finite link check:

```bash
bun dev:docs --port 3333
node scripts/local-docs.js broken-links
node scripts/local-docs.js --print-command
```

`--print-command` shows the exact command without starting a server. `bun dev:docs:local` is a compatibility alias for the same local preview.
`bun dev:docs:down` is disabled while Docker setup is paused; stop the local
foreground preview with Ctrl+C.

## Validate without building apps

```bash
node scripts/generate-docs-inventory.js --check
node scripts/generate-app-seo.js --check
node scripts/docs-audit.js
node --test scripts/docs-audit.test.js scripts/generate-app-seo.test.js
```

Focused tests can use explicit worker bounds. Before broad validation, inspect
`ttr resources status --json` and run heavy commands through
`ttr resources run -- <command>`. Repository policy prohibits local builds and
`bun check`, whose graph can build dependencies. Require relevant test,
type-check, lint, real app builds, and strict Mintlify validation in CI for the
exact source commit. Neither this local path nor a fixture test waives a required
integration check.

## Use remote fixtures deliberately

An approved remote devbox can host isolated Supabase or database-dependent
suites while local editing stays lightweight. Verify the runner's actual host
and checkout; a same-machine container does not offload work. For SQL migrations,
apply to an isolated database and record its exact schema/test evidence. Hosted
Supabase dev/staging services can support read-only application testing when
configured, but they are not interchangeable with a disposable migration test
fixture.

See [Remote devboxes](/build/development-tools/remote-devboxes),
[Local Supabase development](/build/development-tools/local-supabase-development)
for optional isolated fixtures, and the
[active runtime map](/build/devops/active-runtime) for current ownership.

The docs wrapper uses the Node patch pin in `apps/docs/mintlify-version.json`.
Other host versions use an isolated `npx` runtime without changing the host
installation. See [Mintlify runtime compatibility](documenting#mintlify-runtime-compatibility)
for the cancellation mechanism, validation guarantees and pin removal criteria.


Focused Forms metadata/loader tests resolve their mocked Supabase server boundary
from source via `apps/forms/vitest.config.ts`, so they do not require a shared
package build or a Docker database. They cover author noindex settings and
anonymous/protected snapshots; they do not prove live database access.

## Hosted profile await diagnostics

The hosted fixture installs Chromium OS packages through a temporary APT
configuration selecting the runner's signed Ubuntu sources. Unrelated vendor
feeds do not participate; missing Ubuntu sources or package failures stop setup.
Browser downloads run as the runner user. A setup failure before tests produces
no profile acceptance result, even if the terminal artifact is absent.

The disposable hosted Lettin profile fixture retains fixed server read-stage
counts in its existing terminal receipt. Profile actor, bindings, creator and
public-world reads, and workspace layout session, workspace, invitation, list
and navigation reads use the existing CI/explicit-diagnostic gate. Wrappers
preserve results and rethrow the original error; they add no queries, retries,
permission changes or navigation time.

The collector uses its existing owned private log checks and 128-KiB tail. Only
allowlisted stage names, capped started/completed/failed counts and last status
leave the collector, with at most 256 events and explicit tail/event truncation.
Completed and failed read durations retain observed/absent/invalid counts and
maximum milliseconds; a real zero differs from an absent value. Recognized Next
startup, compilation and type-checking display timings remain separate fixed
categories. Display decimals convert exactly at their emitted precision. Missing
compiler timing remains unknown, including webpack paths that emit none. These
aggregate maxima have no request correlation and must not be added into a
critical-path estimate. Each summary has an 8192-byte guard with explicit loss
flags. Timing regressions cover malformed/overflow values and decimal precision.
No raw log lines, paths, request IDs, user data or error messages are retained.
Concurrent reads are not request-correlated: unmatched counts or last status
cannot identify a stalled request, particularly after truncation. Missing stage
observations are inconclusive, and `causeProven` remains false. HTTP 200 with an
unfinished body is not navigation success. Use the bound receipt to narrow the
next investigation; preserve the actual profile assertions, cleanup and exact-head
runtime gate. These diagnostics alone establish neither a causal repair nor
provider or production acceptance.

Failed profile navigation also retains bounded browser observations in
`terminal.results[].navigationDiagnostics`. Request starts, responses, finishes,
failures and frame commits remain separate from body completion and page
`DOMContentLoaded`/`load`. Read capped counts and truncation fields before drawing
conclusions; unobserved requests and frame load stay unknown. The helper records
only safe route classes, local ordinals, relative timings and fixed status fields.
It retains no raw URLs, arbitrary headers, bodies or failure text. The result parser accepts
one versioned text record from the failed profile attempt and preserves its status.
These observations preserve the original navigation deadline and error. They do
not prove a load blocker or justify a retry. Helper and result-summary regressions
cover privacy, framing, limits, cleanup and late callbacks; actual runtime evidence
still requires the exact-head fixture gate.

## Native Wrangler prototype CI validation

Meet's finite `meet-emitted-v1` graph uses two public
`unstable_startWorker` handles and one fresh private registry. Both the original
and restored artifact gates run `node scripts/ci/meet-native-launcher.mjs
"$SOURCE_SHA"`. Each launcher runs all ten original cases and three HTTP hook
controls twice, with distinct private homes, registries, temporary roots and
nonpersistent local storage. The existing three-minute CI watchdog and 30000 ms
per-case deadlines stay in force; duration fit and real binding resolution need
exact-commit CI evidence. Never run it without a fresh sealed emitted artifact.
Pure checks use `node --test scripts/ci/meet-native-admission.test.mjs
scripts/ci/meet-native-lifecycle.test.mjs scripts/ci/meet-native-supplier.test.mjs`.

The app config remains byte-identical, including metadata/normalization paths,
ordered compatibility flags, ESModule rules, self-reference service, local R2,
Images and Live SQLite migration. Normalization paths are provenance, never
ambient-config discovery authority. The authored probe uses an external Live
namespace and the named `MeetingAIProvider` service binding. Acceptance requires
the real emitted Live class's exact 401 and the real named provider's exact 403
with zero HTTP attempts; a route or manually constructed class cannot replace
these cases. Unsupported local resources, registry records or remote auth fail
closed. Do not strip bindings to obtain startup success.

The HTTP fixture claim covers trusted repository app/probe code through each
configured role's outbound hook. App allows one exact bounded central API fixture;
probe allows none. Live controls exercise app default, app named-entrypoint and
probe hooks, including private/loopback/lookalike targets. Hash-pinned SDK generated
helpers, assets/registry/control-plane traffic and Node control paths are trusted
tooling outside that claim. This is neither hostile-code isolation nor whole-process
or TCP confinement. Production access, billing limits and durable stop guards are
unchanged. The app's required provider binding gets only a disposable synthetic
value; no ambient credentials or remote bindings enter the child environment.

Runtime suppliers resolve from Meet's package and then Wrangler's ancestry:
Wrangler 4.151.2 CLI SHA256
`507cd3644d6a53f0d66922d79c04b03557b7d2d0a376d2d906b92ed20812bb30`
and Miniflare 5.20261019.0-beta entry SHA256
`309b8863f0f4c3050e173e945b4c696db8c330cdf3f35f0ecfd8417d75891eaa`.
Both pins are checked before and after SDK load, with preloads rejected and
ownership rechecked across the graph. These attest two entry files, not the
entire transitive installation. Keep the independently pinned normalization
producer separate. A missing or mismatched installation is a blocker; do not
restore dependencies without determining cause and authority.

The graph records each returned public handle before readiness, disposes in
reverse order exactly once and attempts both disposals even when one fails.
Startup/readiness/primary/disposal errors remain separate. The launcher observes
natural child close and stdout/stderr drainage before independently checking
original/copy seals, both SDK work directories, registry removal, foreign sentinel
and temporary-root inventory. A verified retained snapshot precedes removal;
any failed gate retains scratch. Finalization persistence has readback checks.
Private seven-day CI artifacts retain a tar archive of the existing owned
`meet-native-run-*` roots, including hidden `.wrangler` snapshot files, modes,
links and empty directories. Upload only the archive, avoiding the upload action's
hidden-file filter. `meet-native-evidence.test.mjs` executes both selected packaging
commands and compares extracted inventories, including an omission negative;
logs contain bounded statuses rather than fixture credentials. No sweeper, retry,
forced exit or private SDK controller may manufacture closure. SDK internal
cleanup and descendant closure remain UNKNOWN even after public disposal and
natural owned-child close. Pure/source checks do not qualify the emitted graph.

The original validation step also runs the synthetic native Wrangler prototype
unit/runtime suites with file concurrency one and default Node process isolation.
They retain their existing test limits and the same outer three-minute watchdog.
Synthetic qualification is independent of Meet acceptance and does not qualify
Calendar or Apps callers. Historical raw NOTPASS evidence stays unchanged.

Public `Worker.ready` reports proxy readiness, not successful user-Worker linking.
For the four allowlisted returned-Worker startup controls (WASM, logical import
underflow, missing text export and Node builtin), classify the target error only
if observed from a single public `dispose()`: require the exact public name
`MiniflareCoreError [ERR_RUNTIME_FAILURE]`, code `ERR_RUNTIME_FAILURE`, and the
case-specific user-service diagnostic predicate after observation, with fulfilled
proxy readiness. Preserve the observed error C and all primary, ready and disposal failures separately. Do not
invent a ready error or error-object identity, or infer generic disposal success.
Executed evidence qualifies only this isolated harness; caller adoption still
requires separate real-graph acceptance. Existing NOTPASS records stay unchanged.

For the isolated harness, retain a parent-owned sealed cleanup plan. Observe
natural child exit and its actual code/signal (require code 0 and null signal),
then collect residual, original,
copy and foreign-sentinel proofs independently, even when another phase fails.
Before deletion, verify a complete diagnostic snapshot outside every removal
target, including readback and preservation of partial failures. A surviving
pathname or hash cannot recover deleted bytes. If snapshot verification fails,
retain the source and stop deletion. Seal, snapshot, retention, persistence and
removal closure must all pass independently; a receipt or error alone is not
closure. Awaited disposal is not a filesystem fence: Miniflare can schedule
removal through `fireAndForget`. Keep the current finite archives for parent
collection and disposition; do not add automatic sweeps, retries, timeouts,
controllers or private SDK hooks.

The isolated public SDK harness has one intentional pre-return syntax case:
`export default = ;` must produce exactly the owned copied-entry compiler
error `Unexpected "="` at line 1, column 15, with no extra error graph. It may
report `OBSERVABLE_SYNTAX_REJECTION_WITH_CLOSED_CHILD` only after the parent
observes natural child `close`, exit 1 with no signal, drained stdout/stderr and
no spawn/output failure or intervention. Original/copy seals, residual and foreign
file guards, verified retained snapshot, successful owned-file removal and
verified finalization persistence must all succeed first. A failed proof retains
its errors and available evidence; a failed snapshot prevents removal and retains
the source. Internal cleanup and descendant-process closure remain UNKNOWN.
This is a distinct observable negative outcome, not ordinary SDK success or proof
that Wrangler's unobservable internal disposal fulfilled. Every other startup
failure still fails closed. The existing CI watchdog must continue to fail a
stuck stage; no timeout, forced exit or retry can qualify this case.

Synthetic controls live in `native-wrangler-observable.test.mjs`, imported by the
workflow's explicitly named `native-wrangler-runtime.test.mjs` entry. Run that
entry in CI before reviewing the isolated SDK syntax result. Existing Meet,
Calendar and Apps application runtime callers require separate qualification
before adopting this contract.

The dedicated preload-control outcome has a different scope; it grants no generic
missing-Worker waiver. The next bounded CI observation must retain the public
cause chain and proof-phase states, explicit unknown/missing/truncated fields,
and normalized path roles while preserving full diagnostics privately. Do not
infer a parser route or closure from absent public fields. Existing raw NOTPASS
results remain unchanged. Never stage sensitive transcripts; see the CI tooling
reference for supplier evidence.

### Profile request attribution

Only the existing disposable hosted development profile diagnostic gate admits
request attribution. GET HTML document requests receive a fresh 128-bit opaque
`x-lettin-profile-request-id` at proxy entry, replacing any incoming value. The
existing next-intl request-header forwarding carries it into the request context;
the actual response exposes the same ID. Request-scoped memoization reads the
context once for fixed read-stage events. Browser extraction retains only a
validated ID, and `terminal.results[].readCorrelation` joins the single main
profile document response to that ID's bounded events. Redirect IDs cannot stand
in for the destination document. Missing, malformed, duplicate, ambiguous,
cross-attempt or truncated evidence remains unknown; older unattributed aggregates
remain intact. Attributed reads prove only read-stage observations, never renderer,
HTML stream, DOM or page-load completion. Regression coverage lives in
`profile-proxy-diagnostics.test.ts`, `read-diagnostics.test.ts`,
`profile-request-identity.test.ts`, `mail-profile-correlation.test.mjs` and
`mail-profile-result-summary.test.mjs`. Run them in the admitted CI environment;
source inspection and syntax checks do not establish runtime acceptance.
